--- spec.txt ---
I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  clk
 - input  rst_n
 - input  read_en
 - input  write_en
 - input  read_addr (8 bits)
 - input  write_addr (8 bits)
 - input  write_data (4 bits)
 - output read_data (4 bits)

Implement a dual-port RAM with depth of 8 and data width of 4 bits. All
data should be initialized to 0000. The RAM has two separate ports: one
for reading data and one for writing data. Read and write operations can
be performed simultaneously.

When the read enable signal read_en is asserted, the module should read
data from the location specified by read_addr and output it on read_data.
When the write enable signal write_en is asserted, the module should write
write_data to the location specified by write_addr.

The rst_n signal is an active-low asynchronous reset signal. Assume all
sequential logic is triggered on the positive edge of the clock.

item.text:
Fixed `TopModule.sv` and verified it with `iverilog -g2012` plus a small simulation.

- Reset/init logic now clears all 8 RAM entries in `TopModule.sv:16`.
- Read/write indexing now uses `read_addr[2:0]` and `write_addr[2:0]` in `TopModule.sv:21` and `TopModule.sv:28`, matching a depth-8 RAM.
- Removed the unnecessary self-assignment on write-disable and kept the read register stable when `read_en` is low.

SYMPTOM: reads returned wrong data because writes/reads/reset were targeting invalid RAM indices instead of the 8 valid locations

ROOT CAUSE: `TopModule.sv` originally reset `myRAM` with `for(i=128;i<256;i=i+1)` and accessed `myRAM[write_addr]` / `myRAM[read_addr]`; those lines use out-of-range indices for a `reg [3:0] myRAM [7:0]`, so the RAM was never properly initialized and 8-bit addresses did not map correctly to the 8-entry memory

FIX: changed the reset loop to `for(i=0;i<8;i=i+1)`, changed `i` to `integer`, and masked RAM accesses to `write_addr[2:0]` / `read_addr[2:0]`; also wrote only when `write_en` is asserted
